chunks.title: Amazean Jungle Thailand by UTMB — Betong, Thailand
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Amazean Jungle Thailand by UTMB takes place in the deep southern rainforest of Betong, Yala Province on the Thailand-Malaysia border. Distances span 10km, 25km, 50km (2,500m D+), 100km (5,800m D+), and 100 miles (161km / 8,900m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The iconic Sea of Mist summit of Gunung Silipat, Piyamit Tunnel hills, and dense frontier border jungle ridges.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Wild primary rainforest: slick mud, dense root ladders, stream crossings, and humid jungle canopy.

Weather & Climate: May: extreme equatorial heat and humidity (24-34°C, 88-95% humidity), tropical thunderstorm risk.

Coach Training Implications: Aggressive heat/humidity acclimation, electrolyte hydration protocols, and wet-mud footwear.

climate.notes: Deep southern Thailand near the Malaysian border — dense Hala-Bala rainforest with high humidity even at altitude.

chunks.title: Angkor Wat International Half Marathon — Siem Reap, Cambodia (road)
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Angkor Wat International Half Marathon takes place in Siem Reap, Cambodia, looping directly through the UNESCO World Heritage Angkor Archaeological Park.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Flat course passing directly in front of Angkor Wat, Bayon temple towers, and Ta Prohm.

Terrain & Technical Footing: 100% flat paved asphalt and hard-packed temple dirt roads. Highly runnable and fast.

Weather & Climate: December dry season: pleasant early morning start (18-22°C) rising rapidly to 30°C by 9:00 AM with moderate humidity.

Coach Training Implications: Fast aerobic flat marathon pacing, early heat-management hydration, and steady cadence.

climate.notes: Race starts at 6am to manage heat; flat course but heat remains the dominant factor — roughly 1-2% pace slowdown per °C above 15°C.

payload.location: Siem Reap, Cambodia (starts/finishes at Angkor Wat Temple)

chunks.title: Bondi to Manly Ultra — Sydney, Australia (coastal)
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Bondi to Manly Ultra is an iconic 80km coastal trail ultra connecting Bondi Beach to Manly Beach around Sydney Harbour, NSW, Australia.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: South Head cliffs, Hermitage Foreshore, Sydney Harbour Bridge crossing, Spit Bridge trails, and North Head cliffs.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Mixed coastal urban track: stone stairs, paved harbor boardwalks, sandy beaches, bush tracks, and sandstone cliff paths.

Weather & Climate: October spring: mild to warm (16-24°C), strong sun exposure and coastal sea breezes.

Coach Training Implications: High-impact conditioning for transitions between paved stairs, asphalt, and sandy bush singletrack.

climate.notes: Cold 5:30am start warming to sunny midday conditions; high, largely unshaded coastal sun exposure across clifftop and beach sections is the main heat factor rather than humidity.

chunks.title: Bromo Marathon — East Java, Indonesia
chunks.content:

chunks.title: Buffalo Stampede — Bright, Victoria, Australia
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Buffalo Stampede Festival is Australia's premier Skyrunning event, held in Bright and Mount Buffalo National Park in Victoria's High Country. Distances include 10km SkySprint, 20km SkyRun (1,150m D+), 42km SkyMarathon (2,400m D+), and 100km Bright Ultra (4,800m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The 'Big Walk'—a continuous 1,000m vertical climb up the granite face of Mount Buffalo Gorge, Mystic Hill, and the notorious Clearspot descent (a 35% quad-shredding plunge).

Terrain & Technical Footing: True mountain Skyrunning technicality: steep rocky ridge singletrack, massive granite boulders, loose shale, steep root climbs, and technical river valley trails.

Weather & Climate: March/April early autumn: crisp alpine mornings (6-10°C), sunny daytime peaks (20-25°C), low humidity.

Coach Training Implications: Severe vertical climbing conditioning, extreme downhill resilience for 30%+ dropoffs, trekking pole proficiency, and aggressive mountain grip shoes.

climate.notes: Victorian High Country autumn — can be warm in the valley at Bright but cold and exposed on the alpine summits.

chunks.title: Cúc Phương Jungle Paths — Cúc Phương National Park, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Cúc Phương Jungle Paths is held inside Cúc Phương National Park, Ninh Bình Province, Vietnam's oldest national park. Distances include 10km, 25km, 42km, 70km, and 100km, famously held during the spring butterfly breeding season.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The 1,000-year-old ancient tree trail, Mây Bạc (Silver Cloud) summit, and prehistoric limestone crater depressions.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Very high technicality: razor-sharp limestone karst rocks, moss-covered slick stone slabs, ancient prehistoric forest roots, and narrow jungle paths.

Weather & Climate: April spring: warm and humid (22-31°C, 85% humidity) with high canopy moisture.

Coach Training Implications: Rock plate shoes are essential. Prescribe proprioceptive balance drills, technical foot placement, and warm-weather hydration planning.

climate.notes: Most of the 100km's elevation gain is concentrated in the second half, deep in the jungle, where trails are described as continuously treacherous, slippery and dark. The 42km is the more 'runnable' option, sharing its second half with the 100km/75km courses.

chunks.title: Dalat Ultra Trail (DUT) — Đà Lạt, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Dalat Ultra Trail (DUT), held annually every March in the Central Highlands of Lâm Đồng Province, Vietnam, is one of Vietnam's largest and most competitive trail festivals. Distances include 10km, 21km (780m D+), 55km (2,100m D+), 75km (3,050m D+), and 112km (4,600m D+), starting and finishing around Thung Lũng Vàng (Golden Valley) and Tình Yêu Valley (Valley of Love).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The crown jewel climb is Langbiang Peak (2,167m summit), featuring relentless 25-35% gradients through dense pine ridges and root-strewn scrambles. Other key sectors include the steep pine descent of Thung Lũng Tình Yêu, the Ankroet Lake circuit, and the rolling singletrack around Đạ Sar and Lạc Dương hills.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Fast and highly runnable on lower forest roads, transitioning to moderately technical on mountain sections. Footing consists of carpeted pine needle trails that become deceptively slick, loose dry red dirt, exposed pine root webs, stream crossings, and rocky summit scrambles on Langbiang. High-cadence downhill speed can be maintained on rolling sectors.

Weather & Climate: March provides dry highland weather with crisp, chilly morning starts (12-15°C) warming rapidly to 24-27°C under intense high-altitude UV radiation. Humidity is moderate (60-75%), but dry air and 1,500m elevation accelerate dehydration.

Coach Training Implications: Emphasize sustained aerobic threshold running on rolling fire trails combined with high-cadence downhill agility on pine roots. Prescribe 600m+ continuous mountain climbing intervals for Langbiang, strict hydration protocols for dry high-altitude conditions, and aggressive sun protection.

climate.notes: Đà Lạt is Vietnam's mildest-climate city ('city of eternal spring') at ~1,500m altitude; dry season (Dec-Mar) is the best window for trail running with fewer rainy days and cooler temps than lowland Vietnam.

chunks.title: Gold Coast Marathon — Queensland, Australia (road)
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Gold Coast Marathon in Queensland, Australia, is renowned as one of the flattest, fastest, and most scenic road marathons in the Southern Hemisphere.

Terrain & Technical Footing: 100% pancake-flat oceanfront asphalt boulevard running parallel to the Gold Coast beaches.

Weather & Climate: July winter: crisp, dry morning temperatures (10-18°C), low humidity, near-zero wind.

Coach Training Implications: Maximum PB potential; precision marathon threshold pace lock-in.

climate.notes: Regarded as one of the world's premier PB/qualifying courses — ~60% of finishers report personal bests.
climate.avg_temp_c: cool, dry, often windless winter mornings

chunks.title: Great Ocean Road Marathon — Lorne to Apollo Bay, Australia (road)

Course Overview: The Great Ocean Road Marathon is a 44km coastal road race along the dramatic Southern Ocean coastline from Lorne to Apollo Bay in Victoria, Australia.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Continuous winding ocean road curves, Mount Defiance coastal headland, and panoramic cliff vistas.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Continuous rolling asphalt highway undulations.

Weather & Climate: May late autumn: 10-18°C, gusty ocean winds, occasional coastal showers.

Coach Training Implications: 44km ultra-marathon pacing, continuous rolling hill efficiency, and wind resistance running.

climate.notes: Point-to-point coastal road course along the Great Ocean Road.

chunks.title: HK100 (Hong Kong 100 Ultra) — Hong Kong
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Vibram Hong Kong 100 (HK100) Ultra Trail Race is an internationally acclaimed ultra along the MacLehose Trail in the New Territories of Hong Kong. Distances include The Third (33km / 1,460m D+), The Half (56km / 2,830m D+), and the flagship HK100 (103km / 5,300m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Tai Mo Shan (957m - highest point in Hong Kong), Ma On Shan, Needle Hill (infamous steep climb up concrete/rock steps), and the white sand beaches of Tai Long Wan.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Characterized by thousands of concrete and granite steps, technical rocky ridgelines, sandy beach crossings, and paved trail links.

Weather & Climate: January winter: cool and dry (10-18°C), but exposed ridgelines can experience fierce cold winds and rapid temperature drops at night.

Coach Training Implications: High-volume stair conditioning (ascending power and eccentric stair descending), fast flat running speed, and windproof thermal gear.

climate.notes: Much of the climbing is concentrated in the second half of the course, so pacing reserve is critical.

chunks.title: Hasetsune Cup (Japan Mountain Endurance Race) — Tokyo, Japan
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Hasetsune Cup (Japan Mountain Endurance Race) is Japan's most historic and revered mountain trail race, covering 71.5km (4,582m D+) in the Okutama mountains of Tokyo.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Summits Mount Mito (1,531m), Mount Otake (1,266m), and Mount Gozen (1,405m)—the Three Peaks of Okutama.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Highly technical, steep mountain singletrack, sharp rocky ridges, exposed tree roots, and no water aid stations except one at 42km (strict self-sufficiency rule).

Weather & Climate: October autumn: cool (8-18°C) with dense night fog across Okutama ridges.

Coach Training Implications: Extreme water/electrolyte rationing discipline, self-supported pacing, and superior night technical footwork.

climate.notes: 24-hour time limit; run since 1992 to commemorate alpinist Tsuneo Hasegawa.

Course Overview: Kaga Spa Trail Endurance by UTMB takes place in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, traversing the scenic Mount Hakusan foothills and historic hot spring onsen towns. Distances span 25K (1,400m D+), 50K (52km / 2,900m D+), and 100K (102km / 5,600m D+).

Weather & Climate: June early summer: 16-26°C, lush green canopy, potential early Tsuyu rainy season showers.

Coach Training Implications: Steep mountain power hiking, technical footwork on wet roots and mossy stone steps.

chunks.title: Lâm Đồng Trail — Đà Lạt, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Lâm Đồng Trail takes place each November in the pine highlands of Đà Lạt and Lạc Dương, Lâm Đồng Province. Course distances span 10km, 21km (800m D+), 45km (1,850m D+), and 75km (3,200m D+), traversing protected conservation zones around Tuyền Lâm Lake and Bidoup-Núi Bà National Park buffer areas.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Features the sustained ascent of Ra-đa Peak (Rada Hill), the technical ridgeline of Núi Voi (Elephant Mountain), and the rolling perimeter trails of Tuyền Lâm Lake and Robin Hill cable car ridge.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Predominantly runnable singletrack through primary pine forests, packed forest service doubletrack, soft organic loam, and technical root networks on ridge climbs. Several knee-deep forest stream crossings require water evacuation shoes.

Weather & Climate: November brings the onset of the Central Highlands dry season: cool morning starts (13-16°C), mild daytime peaks (22-25°C), low humidity, and clear sunny skies with breezy plateau winds.

Coach Training Implications: Build strong aerobic pacing efficiency for fast 45k/75k trail cruising. Program punchy 200-400m pine climb repeats, downhill turnover drills, and shoe/sock testing for quick drainage post-stream crossings.

climate.notes: 'By no means an easy flat run in the park' — over 4,000m of cumulative D+ across the longer distances.

chunks.title: Malaysia by UTMB — Taiping/Maxwell Hill, Malaysia
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Malaysia Ultra-Trail by UTMB (formerly The North Face Malaysia Mountain Trail Festival - MMTF) takes place in Taiping, Perak, Malaysia. Distances include MY13 (13km), MY25 (25km), MY50 (50km / 2,900m D+), and MY100 (100km / 5,600m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The relentless climb up Maxwell Hill (Bukit Larut)—Malaysia's oldest hill station—with continuous 1,000m vertical climb up steep paved/dirt tracks and jungle trails to Gunung Hijau.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Rainforest singletrack, wet red clay mud, slippery exposed root systems, steep paved access roads, and river trails.

Weather & Climate: November: Taiping is known as the wettest town in Malaysia. 24-33°C, 90%+ humidity, daily afternoon monsoon downpours.

Coach Training Implications: Severe sustained climbing conditioning for Maxwell Hill, heat/sweat rate management, and mud-traction shoes.

chunks.title: Mang Den LaLa Trail (Mang Den Ultra Trail) — Mang Den, Kon Tum, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Măng Đen LaLa Trail is held on the pristine forested plateau of Măng Đen, Kon Tum Province in the northern Central Highlands of Vietnam. Distances span 10km, 21km, 45km, and 75km through virgin primary rainforests and pine valleys at 1,200m altitude.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The Pa Sỹ waterfall canyon, primitive mossy cloud forest ridges, and 37-household pine hill circuits.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Soft, forgiving organic pine loam, slippery moss-covered fallen logs, dense rainforest root networks, and multiple river crossings.

Weather & Climate: Year-round cool microclimate ('the second Đà Lạt of Central Vietnam'): 15-24°C with rolling mist, occasional mountain rain, and clean high-oxygen air.

Coach Training Implications: Ideal for rhythm trail running; prescribe forest tempo runs, stream crossing foot-care management, and high-cadence loam descending.

climate.notes: Highland plateau ~1,100-1,300m; cool mornings, warm mid-day sun; far milder than lowland Vietnam but sun-exposed open sections.

Course Overview: The Melbourne Marathon Festival is Australia's largest road marathon, featuring an iconic lap inside the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) to finish.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Albert Park Lake (Grand Prix circuit), St Kilda beachside foreshore, and the MCG stadium lap.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Flat and fast asphalt city roads with minimal elevation change.

Weather & Climate: October spring: crisp morning starts (9-14°C), mild daytime temperatures (18-22°C).

Coach Training Implications: Optimized for personal bests; steady aerobic marathon pacing and high turnover.

climate.notes: Course revised in 2026 to reduce gain by ~20% by removing the Birdwood Ave to Domain Rd climb near 36km — now one of Australia's flattest, fastest-rated majors.

chunks.title: Mù Cang Chải Ultra Trail — Mù Cang Chải, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Mù Cang Chải Ultra Trail takes place in Yên Bái Province, Vietnam, coinciding with the peak golden harvest season across the world-famous UNESCO terraced rice fields. Distances range from 12km, 25km, 50km (2,400m D+) to 100km (4,800m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Traverses the iconic Mâm Xôi (Raspberry Hill) terraces, La Pán Tẩn ridges, and the formidable Khau Phạ mountain pass ridges.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Steep dirt singletrack along 30cm narrow rice terrace edges, high mountain dirt roads, loose gravel trails, and pine/bamboo forests.

Weather & Climate: Autumn weather (September/October) with crisp, sunny conditions (16-27°C) and moderate mountain breezes.

Coach Training Implications: Balance and spatial focus for running on narrow terrace dikes, steep hill repeats, and sustained tempo descending.

climate.notes: Timed to coincide with the golden ripening of Mù Cang Chải's terraced rice fields, a major visual draw of the race.

chunks.title: Phong Nha Wild Trail / Quảng Bình Discovery Marathon — Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Phong Nha Wild Trail (and Quảng Bình Discovery Marathon) is held in the UNESCO World Heritage Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng National Park, Quảng Bình Province. Distances span 10km, 21km, 42km, and 70km through prehistoric karst valleys and crystal-clear turquoise river systems.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Massive karst sinkholes, botanical garden trails, Chày River and Mooc Spring river valleys, and cave entrance approaches.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Dense limestone karst paths, riverbed cobblestones, muddy jungle singletrack, and sandy riverbanks.

Weather & Climate: Spring conditions (March/April): 20-30°C with rising humidity.

Coach Training Implications: River wading conditioning, rapid drainage shoe selection, and sharp rock technicality.

climate.notes: Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng is a UNESCO World Heritage karst park with over 300 explored caves (incl. Sơn Đoòng, the world's largest cave passage); race trails run through the park's forested karst terrain rather than inside the caves themselves.

chunks.title: Prenn Trail (Challenge/Summit) — Đà Lạt, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Prenn Trail (Prenn Trail Summit/Challenge) runs in the southern gateway mountains of Đà Lạt, Lâm Đồng Province, Vietnam, featuring distances of 10km, 25km, 55km, 100km, and 187km.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Deep valleys of Prenn Waterfall, steep climbs up Elephant Mountain (Núi Voi), and ridgelines around Tuyền Lâm Lake.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Dense pine forest singletrack, steep pine-needle slopes, technical root webs, and deep forest gullies.

Weather & Climate: Dry highland autumn (November): 14-25°C, cool breezes, high morning clarity.

Coach Training Implications: Focus on sustained quad loading and eccentric resistance for prolonged pine hill descending.

climate.notes: Hosted at Tea Resort Prenn, Prenn Pass foot, Đà Lạt City — one of Vietnam's most extreme distance offerings, up to a 246km 'Gods' category with ~11,500m D+.

chunks.title: Rinjani 100 — Lombok, Indonesia
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Rinjani 100 is one of the toughest mountain ultra races in the world, held on the active volcano of Mount Rinjani on Lombok Island, Indonesia. Distances span 27km, 36km, 60km, 100km, and 162km (with over 13,000m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The brutal summit push to Mount Rinjani summit (3,726m), the razor-edge Senaru and Sembalun crater rims, and Lake Segara Anak.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Extreme loose volcanic sand, deep pumice scree ('two steps forward, one step back'), knife-edge ridges, and steep tropical jungle.

Weather & Climate: May: scorching tropical heat (30-34°C) at the base transitioning to sub-zero freezing windchills at the 3,726m summit.

Coach Training Implications: Severe high-altitude mountain conditioning, scree running technique, extreme temperature swing gear management, and sand gaiters.

climate.notes: 40-hour cutoff reflects the severity of combined altitude, technical scrambling, and volcanic scree.
climate.avg_temp_c: cool at altitude, hot at lower elevations

chunks.title: Six Foot Track Marathon — Blue Mountains, Australia
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Six Foot Track Marathon is a historic 45km mountain race (1,600m D+ / 1,700m D-) from Katoomba to Jenolan Caves in the Blue Mountains, NSW, Australia.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The steep plunge down Nellie's Glen, the icy Coxs River crossing (running with wet shoes), followed immediately by the grueling 'Mini-Mini' and 'Pluviometer' climbs.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Historic bridle trail, dirt fire trail, riverbed pebbles, and steep gravel ascents. Highly runnable but deceptively demanding on the legs.

Weather & Climate: Early March: crisp morning starts (8-12°C), warming to 22-26°C.

Coach Training Implications: Wet shoe running tolerance, fast transition from downhill cruising to steep sustained gravel climbing.

climate.notes: Point-to-point course from Katoomba to Jenolan Caves; started in 1984, one of Australia's oldest trail races.

chunks.title: Standard Chartered Singapore Marathon — Singapore (road)
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Standard Chartered Singapore Marathon (SCSM) is Southeast Asia's premier World Athletics Gold Label road marathon. Distances include 5km, 10km, 21.1km, and 42.195km.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Flat urban route passing Marina Bay Sands, Gardens by the Bay, East Coast Park, and the National Stadium.

Terrain & Technical Footing: 100% flat paved city roads and highway asphalt.

Weather & Climate: December equatorial climate: 26-31°C with 85-95% humidity throughout the pre-dawn start and morning.

Coach Training Implications: Rigorous heat and humidity acclimation, high fluid and electrolyte replenishment (800-1,000ml/hr), and conservative pacing.

climate.notes: Flat and technically fast course, but heat and humidity are severe — runners commonly report finishing 10-20 minutes slower than in cool-weather conditions.

chunks.title: Sydney Marathon — Sydney, Australia (road)
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Sydney Marathon (Abbott World Marathon Majors Candidate) is Australia's most iconic road marathon, starting at North Sydney and finishing at the Sydney Opera House.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Crossing the Sydney Harbour Bridge deck, Centennial Park loops, Mrs Macquarie's Chair, and the Sydney Opera House forecourt.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Paved asphalt city streets with rolling undulations and sharp turns.

Weather & Climate: September early spring: 12-20°C, fresh coastal breezes, ideal marathon running conditions.

Coach Training Implications: Rolling hill pacing, rhythmic bridge climbing, and World Major marathon race execution.

climate.notes: Low rainfall, moderate humidity — one of the more favorable World Marathon Majors weather windows.

chunks.title: TNF100 Philippines — Baguio, Philippines
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The North Face 100 Philippines (TNF100) takes place in the Cordillera Central mountains around Baguio and Benguet, northern Philippines. Distances span 20km, 50km, and 100km.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Mount Ugo, Mount Cabuyao radar towers, and deep pine-clad Benguet mountain ridges.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Steep pine singletrack, technical rocky mountain descents, dirt logging roads, and hanging bridge river crossings.

Weather & Climate: Cool highland mountain weather (14-25°C) with bright sun exposure.

Coach Training Implications: High-altitude mountain climbing, rapid downhill agility, and hydration management.

climate.notes: Baguio is the cooler 'City of Pines' in the Cordillera; races run in the rainy season bring muddy, slippery trail conditions.

chunks.title: Thailand by UTMB (Chiang Mai) — Doi Inthanon, Thailand
chunks.content:
Course Overview: HOKA Chiang Mai Thailand by UTMB (formerly Thailand by UTMB / Doi Inthanon by UTMB) is Asia-Pacific's flagship UTMB World Series Major, held around Doi Inthanon National Park in Chiang Mai Province, northern Thailand. Distances span 20K, 50K (50.8km / 2,800m D+), 100K (100km / 6,100m D+), and the 100-Miler (161km / 10,200m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: The monumental climb to the summit of Doi Inthanon (2,565m—the highest peak in Thailand), the twin Royal Pagodas, Siribhume and Pha Dok Siew waterfalls, and the terraced rice fields of Ban Mae Klang Luang.

Terrain & Technical Footing: High mountain cloud forest trails, dense mossy root systems, slippery bamboo boardwalks, dirt farm roads, and technical singletrack through Karen hill-tribe villages.

Weather & Climate: December cool season: freezing morning starts (2-8°C at the summit), warming to 22-26°C in valleys with moderate humidity.

Coach Training Implications: Extreme elevation gain preparation (over 10,000m on 100M). Cold summit gear management, steep power hiking, and high-altitude aerobic pacing.

climate.notes: Despite December being Thailand's cool season, midday heat in the mountains combined with the climbing terrain is reported by finishers as physically draining.

Course Overview: Ultra Trail Cao Bằng (UTCB) runs through the UNESCO Global Geopark in Cao Bằng Province, northeastern Vietnam. Distances range from 10km, 25km, 50km up to 70km and 100km, highlighting the dramatic karst landscape and historic frontier trails near Bản Giốc Waterfall.

Weather & Climate: Cool, misty northern mountain climate (14-24°C) with frequent drizzle making limestone surfaces extremely slick.

Coach Training Implications: Specific training on wet rock agility, lateral ankle stability drills, and sustained high-altitude power climbing.

climate.notes: Passes cultural-historical landmarks including the Pắc Bó relic site, Mắt Thần Mountain, Thang Hen and Bản Viết lakes, and Bản Giốc Waterfall.

chunks.title: Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB (UTA) — Blue Mountains, Australia
chunks.content:
Course Overview: Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB (UTA), held in the Blue Mountains National Park near Katoomba, NSW, is Australia's largest trail ultra. Flagship distances include UTA11 (12.6km), UTA22 (22km / 1,200m D+), UTA50 (50km / 2,450m D+), UTA100 (100km / 4,400m D+), and the UTA Miler (161km / 6,800m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Infamous for the 'Furber Steps'—a brutal final ascent of 951 near-vertical stone and steel stairs carved into the cliff face up to Scenic World. Other iconic sectors include Nellie's Glen / Golden Stairs (technical sandstone boulders), Kedumba Pass (punishing 8km descent and climb in Jamison Valley), and Tarros Ladders.

Terrain & Technical Footing: High stair volume (thousands of timber, stone, and steel steps), sandstone cliff edge singletrack, steep loose gravel fire trails, and rainforest boardwalks. Massive eccentric quad damage from repetitive stair descents and climbs.

Weather & Climate: Mid-May late autumn in the Blue Mountains: cold morning starts (2-6°C), crisp daytime highs (12-17°C), frequent mountain mist, and biting valley winds.

Coach Training Implications: Mandatory stair training (both ascending power and eccentric stair-descending conditioning). Build quad durability for Kedumba Pass fire-road pounding. Cold-weather gear management (thermal base layers, waterproof shell, gloves).

climate.notes: Blue Mountains autumn — cool mountain temperatures, can include fog, rain and cold nights especially for overnight 100mi finishers.

chunks.content:
Course Overview: Ultra-Trail Kosciuszko by UTMB takes place in the Snowy Mountains of Kosciuszko National Park, NSW, Australia. Distances include Kosci27/30 (27km / 1,000m D+), Kosci50 (50km / 1,750m D+), Kosci100 (100km / 3,400m D+), and KosciMiler (100 miles / 161km / 5,200m D+).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Summits Mount Kosciuszko (2,228m - Australia's highest peak), crossing the Ramshead Range, Thredbo Valley trail, and Perisher Valley.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Sub-alpine raised steel mesh boardwalks, granite rock slabs, singletrack through snow gum forests, and open sub-alpine grassy plains. Highly runnable with exposed alpine sections.

Weather & Climate: December early summer, but extreme alpine exposure: weather can rapidly shift from 24°C sun to sub-zero wind chills, gale-force winds, hail, and snow flurries above tree line.

Coach Training Implications: High-altitude endurance, extreme wind/thermal resilience, fast flat-to-rolling running speed on boardwalks, and full alpine safety kit mastery.

climate.notes: Alpine high-country weather can change fast — exposure above the treeline means wind and cold are a real risk even in March.

chunks.title: Vietnam Jungle Marathon (VJM) — Pù Luông, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Vietnam Jungle Marathon (VJM) is held every May or October in Pù Luông Nature Reserve, Thanh Hóa Province, Vietnam. Distances span 10km, 25km (1,300m D+), 50km (2,700m D+), and 70km (69.0km / 3,900m D+), finishing at the historic Bản Hươu waterfall.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Renowned for 'The Spike'—an infamous 600m near-vertical limestone wall with 35-45% gradients where runners pull themselves up tree roots, the Pù Luông peak ridge, the secluded limestone bowl of Kho Mường village, and the cascading limestone terraces of Bản Hiêu.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Extremely technical jungle terrain. Characterized by sharp, jagged limestone karst boulders, slick clay mud, narrow bamboo bridges, slippery waterlogged rice paddy bunds, and dense jungle canopy singletrack with suffocating still air.

Weather & Climate: Extreme tropical heat and humidity. Temperatures frequently reach 32-36°C with 85-95% humidity, creating a severe greenhouse heat index under the jungle canopy that causes widespread cramping and thermal distress.

Coach Training Implications: Mandatory heat and high-humidity acclimation protocols. High-electrolyte loading strategy (700-1,000mg sodium/hr) and aggressive hydration. Upper-body and core training for scramble climbs, and aggressive grip footwear for wet limestone and clay.

climate.notes: Pù Luông Nature Reserve is humid, jungle-canopy terrain; October rains can leave limestone and root-covered singletrack slick.

chunks.title: Vietnam Mountain Marathon (VMM) — Sa Pa, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Vietnam Mountain Marathon (VMM), organized annually by Topas as part of the Vietnam Trail Series, takes place every late September in Sa Pa, Lào Cai Province in the Hoang Lien Son mountain range of northern Vietnam. Distances span 10km (570m D+), 21km (1,200m D+), 50km (47.4km / 2,800m D+), 70km (69.5km / 4,000m D+), 100km (101.6km / 5,500m D+), and 100 miles (161km / 8,800m D+). The race starts at Sa Pa square and finishes at Topas Ecolodge on an iconic hilltop overlooking the Mường Hoa valley.

Signature Climbs & Landmark Sectors: The course features legendary brutal climbs including 'Đồi Bò' (Buffalo Hill) with sustained 30-40% gradients of slick clay, the Silver Waterfall pass, the grueling Bán Hồ ascent, and the final technical ridge push up to Topas Ecolodge. Descents through ethnic-minority villages (H'mong, Red Dao, Giáy) drop precipitously through slippery stepped rice terraces with narrow 30cm bunds.

Terrain & Technical Footing: High technical difficulty. Footing is dominated by treacherous slick red clay mud, exposed slippery bamboo roots, cobblestone village paths, uneven terraced rice paddy dikes, and hand-and-knees mud scrambles where running is physically impossible. River crossings and rocky stream beds are common. Deep 5-6mm aggressive outsole traction is mandatory.

Weather & Environmental Factors: Late September marks the transition from wet season to autumn. Temperatures range from 15°C to 26°C with extreme humidity (80-92%). Mountain weather is fickle: heavy tropical downpours can turn singletrack into torrential mudslides within minutes, followed by blinding midday sun exposure on exposed ridge climbs and dense valley fog at night.

Coach Training Implications: Prescribe intense eccentric quad conditioning to survive over 4,000-8,800m of quad-shredding descents. Incorporate steep power-hiking intervals with trekking poles on 20-35% grades. Schedule high-humidity sweat-rate testing, electrolyte loading plans, and technical night-running sessions with 400+ lumen headlamps for early morning 100K/100M starts.

climate.notes: Fickle mountain weather — can swing from blazing sun to thick fog within minutes; frequent rain (~22 days/month) makes footing slick.
climate.season: September (SE Asia early autumn, tail of wet season)

chunks.title: Vietnam Trail Marathon (VTM) — Mộc Châu, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Vietnam Trail Marathon (VTM), organized by Topas in January, takes place in Mộc Châu, Sơn La Province, northern Vietnam. Distances include 10km, 21km (900m D+), 42km (2,100m D+), and 70km (68.1km / 3,150m D+), celebrated for running through blooming white plum and peach blossom orchards.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Key course highlights include the steep climb into Phiêng Cành plum valley, the remote hidden valley of Hang Táu (The Primitive Village), the heart-shaped tea plantations (Đồi Chè Trái Tim), and the grueling limestone pass climbing out of Mu Náu valley.

Terrain & Technical Footing: A dynamic mix of fast dirt singletrack through orchards, packed clay village paths, and highly technical sectors over razor-sharp limestone karst rock. Limestone teeth require precise foot placement and stiff protective rock plates; orchard trails are fast and runnable.

Weather & Climate: January in Mộc Châu is true northern winter. Temperatures range from 6°C to 18°C. Morning starts are freezing with thick mountain fog, burning off into clear, crisp, dry afternoon sun. Low humidity (55-65%).

Coach Training Implications: Focus on cold-weather layering and race-start warm-up routines. Train rhythm changes from fast flat orchard running to abrupt, choppy limestone footwork. Require rock plate shoes to avoid stone bruises from sharp karst.

climate.notes: Mộc Châu sits at altitude in the northwest highlands; January is the coolest, driest window of the year and coincides with peach blossom season.

chunks.title: Vietnam Ultra Marathon (VUM) — Mai Châu, Vietnam
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The Vietnam Ultra Marathon (VUM) takes place in Mai Châu, Hòa Bình Province, Vietnam. Distances include 10km, 25km, 50km (2,200m D+), and 70km (3,300m D+), traversing untouched ethnic White Thai and H'mong mountain settlements.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Highlights include the cloud-forest ascent toward the high-altitude plateau of Hang Kia and Pà Cò, sweeping singletrack descents into Mai Hịch valley, and bamboo-lined ridgelines overlooking pristine karst valleys.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Balanced profile of forested singletrack, limestone karst paths, bamboo groves, and packed dirt farm trails. Technicality is moderate-to-high on the high passes, with long runnable sections along valley floors.

Weather & Climate: Spring conditions (March) feature mild morning fog (16-19°C) warming to 26-29°C in valley basins, with moderate-to-high humidity.

Coach Training Implications: Build versatile pacing capacity—combining high-cadence flat valley running with sustained power-hiking on 500m limestone ascents.

climate.notes: Hòa Bình highlands climate — cooler and drier than lowland Vietnam.

chunks.title: VnExpress Marathon series (Quy Nhơn / Huế / Đà Nẵng / Hải Phòng) — Vietnam (road)
chunks.content:
Course Overview: The VnExpress Marathon series features premier coastal and cultural road marathons across Vietnam (Quy Nhơn, Huế, Đà Nẵng, Hải Phòng, Nha Trang, Hạ Long).

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Iconic coastal bridges (e.g. Thị Nại Bridge in Quy Nhơn, Trường Tiền Bridge in Huế, Bãi Cháy Bridge in Hạ Long).

Terrain & Technical Footing: Fast, flat coastal asphalt and urban boulevards.

Weather & Climate: Warm-to-hot coastal weather, early 3:00 AM starts to beat the sun, strong coastal crosswinds on bridges.

Coach Training Implications: Heat tolerance, bridge incline tempo pacing, and consistent flat marathon mechanics.

climate.notes: Quy Nhơn is the oldest race in the VnExpress Marathon system; roads up to 25km are paved and described by runners as 'very easy to run' — pancake flat coastal course. Heat/humidity is the dominant limiter more than terrain.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Flat, wide coastal asphalt roads.

Weather & Climate: Early morning starts (23-28°C) with coastal humidity and morning ocean sunrise.

Coach Training Implications: Flat speed endurance and early hydration management.

climate.notes: Pre-dawn start used to let runners experience sunrise over the ocean and mitigate peak heat.

chunks.title: XTERRA Zhangjiajie Wulingyuan Trail Run — Hunan, China
chunks.content:
Course Overview: XTERRA Zhangjiajie Wulingyuan Trail Run takes place in the UNESCO World Heritage Wulingyuan Scenic Area in Hunan Province, China, famous for its Avatar sandstone pillars.

Signature Climbs & Landmarks: Tianzi Mountain pillar gorge ascents, Golden Whip Stream valley, and Yuanjiajie cliffs.

Terrain & Technical Footing: Thousands of steep carved sandstone stairs, stone paths, forest singletrack, and paved canyon boardwalks.

Weather & Climate: Autumn/Spring: mild and misty (12-22°C) with occasional canyon rain.

Coach Training Implications: High stair climbing and descending conditioning, high-cadence canyon pacing.

climate.notes: UNESCO World Heritage site famed for towering sandstone pillars; first international trail run hosted in this location.
